description: The bar chart presents a comparative evaluation of the F1 Score (%) across six multivariate anomaly detection datasets—SMD, PSM, SWaT, SMAP, MSL, and WADI—for four variants of the MADLLM model, as described in the paper “MADLLM: Multivariate Anomaly Detection via Pre-trained LLMs.” The vertical axis quantifies performance from 60% to 100% in 10% increments, using a linear scale, while the horizontal axis organizes the datasets in fixed order. For each dataset, four adjacent bars represent: MADLLM (green), MADLLM without prompt pool (blue), MADLLM without feature embedding (purple), and MADLLM without skip embedding (orange), as indicated by the legend below the chart. Across all datasets, the full MADLLM (green) consistently achieves the highest F1 Score: approximately 95% on SMD, over 95% on PSM, around 92% on SWaT, 94% on SMAP, 88% on MSL, and 74% on WADI. The ablated versions show varying degrees of performance degradation: on SMD, the purple variant (w/o feature embedding) drops to ~85%; on PSM, the blue variant (w/o prompt pool) falls sharply to ~77%; on SWaT, all variants remain above 90%, with the blue variant at ~83%; on SMAP, the orange variant (w/o skip embedding) plummets to ~67%; on MSL, the blue variant drops to ~69%; and on WADI, the purple variant falls to ~62%. The chart visually emphasizes the importance of each component in the full MADLLM architecture, with the green bars consistently outperforming the ablated configurations, particularly in datasets like SMAP and WADI where the absence of skip or feature embeddings leads to substantial performance drops.
caption_used: The bar chart illustrates the F1 Score percentages of different MADLLM configurations across various datasets. The horizontal axis lists the categories, which are datasets labeled as SMD, PSM, SWaT, SMAP, MSL, and WADI. The vertical axis represents the F1 Score in percentage, ranging from 60% to 100% with regular tick intervals marked every 10 percentage points, indicating a linear scale. For each dataset, four bars are grouped together, each representing a different MADLLM configuration: 'MADLLM' in green, 'MADLLM w/o prompt pool' in blue, 'MADLLM w/o feature embedding' in purple, and 'MADLLM w/o skip embedding' in orange. In the SMD dataset, the green bar is the tallest, reaching approximately 95%, while the purple bar is the shortest, at around 85%. For the PSM dataset, the green bar exceeds 90%, while the blue bar is significantly shorter, at approximately 70%. The SWaT dataset shows a consistent trend, with all bars exceeding 90%, and the green bar being the tallest. In SMAP, the green bar reaches approximately 94%, with the other bars significantly lower, with orange being the shortest, at approximately 60%. The MSL dataset shows the green bar as the tallest, at approximately 90%, while the blue bar is the shortest, at around 65%. Finally, for WADI, the green bar is the tallest, at approximately 80%, while the purple bar is the shortest, at around 60%. A legend is placed at the bottom of the plot.
